source_text: Aio enim: Quid ergo suum diabolus cognoscit in sexibus, ut fructum eorum, sicut dicis, iure possideat? Diversitatem? Sed haec in corporibus est, quae Deus fecit. Commixtionem? Sed non minus benedictionis, quam institutionis privilegio vindicatur. An forte ipsam fecunditatem? Sed ipsa est instituti causa coniugii. Quid hic ergo novum fuit; quid a superiore quam probaveras conclusione dissentiens, quod post laudem vituperandum putares? Certe nihil: ac per hoc quid de tam foeda varietate colligitur? Cum a me videlicet disputatio innovata non sit, a te vero sit aestimatio meorum dictorum permutata, teterrimam esse intentionem tuam, et rationem imbecillam.
pass_a_gloss: For I say: What therefore does the devil recognize as his own in the sexes, so that, as you say, he may rightly possess their fruit? Difference? But this is in the bodies which God made. Mingling? But it is claimed by the privilege of blessing no less than of institution. Or perhaps fertility itself? But that itself is the cause of the institution of marriage. What therefore was new here; what dissenting from the earlier conclusion which you had approved, that after praise you thought should be blamed? Certainly nothing: and through this what is gathered from so foul a variation? Since, namely, the disputation was not renewed by me, but the estimation of my sayings was changed by you, your intention is most foul, and the reasoning weak.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: For I say: “What, then, does the devil recognize as his own in the sexes, so that, as you say, he rightly possesses their offspring? Their difference? But that exists in the bodies God made. Their union? But it is defended by the privilege of God’s blessing no less than by his institution. Or perhaps fertility itself? But that is the very reason marriage was instituted.” What was new here? What disagreed with the previous conclusion you had approved, so that you thought you should blame it after praising it? Certainly nothing. What follows, then, from such disgusting inconsistency? Clearly, since my argument has not changed while your assessment of my words has altered, your intention is utterly foul and your reasoning weak.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
